Class 2: Codes and patterns

Use repeating groups, internal gaps and picture rules; older grades also separate linked number rules.

ExplorePosition and order

How many boats are to the left of the encircled boat?

  1. A2
  2. B1
  3. C4
  4. D3

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Do not count the encircled boat itself. Count only the boats before it.

Answer & method
Answer A: 2

The encircled boat is 3rd from the left. The number of boats before it is 3 - 1 = 2.

Try more in game →

ReasonNumber patterns

The IN number enters the rule machine. What number comes OUT at '?'?

  1. A60
  2. B53
  3. C48
  4. D45

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Apply the first part of the rule to the IN number, then apply the second part to that result.

Answer & method
Answer C: 48

Start with 9, multiply by 5 to get 45, then add 3 to get 48.

StretchVisual reasoning

Which badge fits the '?' at row 3, column 3 of the 3 by 3 badge grid?

  1. APicture A
  2. BPicture B
  3. CPicture C
  4. DPicture D

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Check across the row to find the outer shape, then check down the column to find the inner mark.

Answer & method
Answer A: Picture A

Across row 3 every badge has a square shape, and down column 3 every badge has a ring, giving a square with a ring.

For grown-ups

Ideas to practise

  • Place value. A digit has a different value in each position. Count the places from the right.
  • Position and order. Use the given left-to-right order, then count or locate a neighbour.
  • Shapes and their properties. Count straight sides and corners carefully. A curved edge is not a straight side.
  • Solids and nets. Follow which faces meet when folded. A face touching another in the net cannot be opposite it.
  • Repeating patterns. Find the smallest repeating group and continue that group.
  • Calendars. Read the weekday headings. A week has seven days; count intervals, not both endpoints.
  • Number patterns. Look for the same change between neighbouring numbers.
  • Sorting by a rule. Check which object does not share the named property.
  • Coding and decoding. Apply the stated code consistently to each letter.
  • Possible combinations. Match each choice in the first group with every allowed choice in the second.
  • Visual reasoning. Track the position, orientation and markings, not just the outline. Check every part of a picture.

A game mission has 8 untimed questions. Only the game saves choices and hints. A finished mission earns one launch charge and participation towards the Right solar panel in Outer Planet Voyager. The chapter goal is 8 different questions in finished sets; hints and wrong answers count as participation, not mastery. Some craft systems link more than one chapter.

Using the feedback

Learning reports distinguish hinted answers from independent first choices. They consider up to 20 recent different, unhinted questions per skill and level, and wait for at least five before suggesting extra practice. Repeating the same question does not add evidence. Reports are practice evidence, not IQ scores, diagnoses, ranks or predictions of competition results.

Ask the learner to explain a drawing or check with objects too. Choose Explore or an earlier chapter when a step feels too large.

Sources & limits

The grade topics use SOF IMO Class 2 published topic syllabus as their primary reference. The SOF sample and CREST previous-year paper below informed representations and reasoning demands. Providers have different topic boundaries; their syllabi are not interchangeable.

  • Sample, not an administered paper: SOF IMO Class 2 sample, 2026-27
  • Previous-year paper: CREST CMO Class 2 previous-year paper, 2023-24 Set A

Questions, diagrams, picture choices, hints and explanations are original Otterly work, not copied paper questions or publisher artwork. No Olympiad provider is affiliated with or endorses Space Academy. This is not complete exam preparation; follow classroom teaching and check the current official syllabus too. Independent educator review is still needed for difficulty and breadth.

Content and coverage notes. To report a confusing question, describe the grade, chapter, level and question on the contact page. Do not send children’s personal information.
